visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly depicts the nested circles sharing a common point and places the derivation beside that geometry, though it over-shades the whole disk instead of only alternating annular regions, whereas Lesson 2 uses largely decorative overlapping-circle graphics that do not match the required common-point/nested-circle configuration at all.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired quiz gate after act_derivation with a real question, plausible options, and a marked correct answer, whereas Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2’s narration is more natural and consistently speaks the math clearly, while Lesson 1 has several awkward/ambiguous formula readings like “two-k squared,” “four-k-squared,” and “two-n-squared plus n” that could confuse listeners even though it is more concise.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 at least times most major visual changes near the narration that references them, despite some early or overly broad cues, whereas Lesson 2 provides no beat/timing cues at all despite frequent references to slides, steps, and visuals, making its on-screen synchronization unsupported.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is more conceptually faithful to the non-concentric, internally tangent nested-circle geometry and clearly emphasizes the rings-to-circles distinction, while Lesson 1 incorrectly calls the circles concentric despite sharing a circumference point, an impossible setup that could mislead learners even though its area algebra is correct.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a cleaner, more legible, consistently styled notebook layout with well-sized text and centered compositions, while Lesson 1 is denser, less balanced, has overlapping/competing elements, and shows raw LaTeX-style dollar-sign labels in the mid-lesson frame.

aggregator.explanation: The six dimensions are split 3–3, but the confidence-weighted balance slightly favors Lesson 1. Lesson 1 wins strongly on interactivity, visual accuracy, and synchronization: it has a functioning quiz gate, better-matched geometry, and actual timing cues. Lesson 2 wins narration, conceptual accuracy, and polish, with especially strong polish and a clearer treatment of the non-concentric tangent-circle concept. However, Lesson 2’s lack of interactivity and timing support, plus inaccurate decorative visuals, are major production weaknesses. Overall, Lesson 1 has the narrow edge despite Lesson 2’s cleaner presentation and stronger conceptual narration.
